title: Study of Carbohydrate Composition in Couch Grass Underground Organs
author: Momot, Tetyana
license_note: Zenodo record metadata license field: cc-by-4.0
materials: Aqueous solutions of PS are precipitated with a 1% solution of aluminum sulfate with the formation of pectates. The results of the research indicate that in rhizomes and roots of couch grass, the content of PS is (6.57±0.
%, and the content of WSP is (5.85±0.

steps.title: Prepare aqueous extracts
steps.instruction: Combine 30 g crushed dry rhizomes and roots with 250 mL hot purified water, infuse for 24 h, filter, add 100 mL hot purified water to the residue, repeat the extraction 3–5 times, combine all filtrates and evaporate the pooled extract to a final volume of 15 mL.

steps.title: Precipitate polysaccharides with ethanol
steps.instruction: Add 30 mL of 95 % ethanol to 10 mL of the concentrated aqueous extract; observe formation of floating lamellar clots that settle, indicating polysaccharide precipitation.

steps.title: Filter polysaccharide sediment
steps.instruction: Filter the ethanol‑precipitated sediment and collect the solid for subsequent reactions.

steps.title: Hydrolyze sediment for reducing sugars
steps.instruction: Transfer the filtered sediment to a test tube, add 5 mL diluted hydrochloric acid, and boil for 30 min; then allow the mixture to cool.

steps.title: Test hydrolysate with Fehling's reagent
steps.instruction: Add 10 mL Fehling's reagent to the cooled hydrolysate and boil again; the appearance of a brick‑red precipitate confirms the presence of reducing (neutral) sugars.

steps.title: Determine WSP and PS gravimetrically
steps.instruction: Dry and weigh the polysaccharide and pectin precipitates obtained from the ethanol and Fehling procedures; calculate the percentages of water‑soluble polysaccharides (WSP) and pectin substances (PS) using the gravimetric method.

steps.title: Prepare samples for GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Extract total and free sugars from the plant material under the required conditions, add sorbitol solution as an internal standard, and derivatize the sugars to their aldonitrile acetate derivatives.

steps.title: Run GC‑MS monosaccharide analysis
steps.instruction: Inject the derivatized samples into an Agilent 6890N/5973 GC‑MS equipped with an HP‑5ms capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm × 0.25 µm); identify monosaccharides by comparison with standards and the NIST 02 mass‑spectra library.
